newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares end down, gripped by rate worries.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares end down, gripped by rate worries.

text.p: Dutch blue chips ended a session of largely range-bound trading down almost one percent on Wednesday with the market gripped by interest worries.
The AEX finished 6.69 points or 0.90 percent lower at 735.04, its third consecutive lower close, having started the day marginally down at 741.32.
Dealers said options-led selling drove the AEX down in early trade, as investors stepping out of index calls prompted basket selling.
It briefly pared losses on renewed buyer interest at midday, helped by support from firmer guilder bonds.

However the AEX resumed its downtrend after a slightly higher than expected U.S. February consumer prices gain, although economists said it did not significantly change the prospects of a hike in U.S. rates when the Federal Open Market Committee meets next week.
"Sentiment is down generally because of the growing rate worries," one dealer said.
He said early gains on Wall Street before the Amsterdam market closed had done little to dispel the negative sentiment.
Rate worries targeted index-heavy financials, with ABN Amro falling 1.10 guilders to 128.90 and ING off 1.90 at 71.80 guilders.

Steel and aluminium maker Hoogovens was among the gainers, adding 3.10 guilders to 91.70 on news of a possible merger between German steel giants Thyssen and Krupp-Hoesch, which was seen as reducing European market overcapacity.

"In the long run, though, this could be a very bad move for Hoogovens because Krupp-Thyssen synergies could help them to produce so cheaply they elbow Hoogovens out of major markets," one dealer said.
Recorded music company Polygram made good recent losses, surging 5.80 guilders to 94.80 on news U2's new album "Pop" was selling well, dealers said.
Foods group Nutricia was well down at 286.60, sliding 7.70 guilders due to a critical report in the latest issue of Business Week, which questioned its long-term prospects, dealers said.
On the AMX MidCap index builder HBG added 3.50 guilders to 425.00 ahead of 1996 results due on Tuesday, but sector peer Volker Stevin lost 7.50 to 204.00 as investors took profits after recent gains.
The AMX ended the session down 13.87 points or 1.25 percent at 1093.92. REUTER/LVL
